claims.quote: We have high towers; the highest about half a mile in height; and some of them likewise set upon high mountains; so that the vantage of the hill with the tower is in the highest of them three miles at least.
claims.description: Towers half a mile tall, and taller when built on mountains, are used for observing weather and other phenomena.

claims.quote: And amongst them we have a water which we call Water of Paradise, being, by that we do to it made very sovereign for health, and prolongation of life.
claims.description: A specially treated water is claimed to prolong life and restore health.

claims.quote: We have also great and spacious houses where we imitate and demonstrate meteors; as snow, hail, rain, some artificial rains of bodies and not of water, thunders, lightnings; also generations of bodies in air; as frogs, flies, and divers others.
claims.description: Artificial snow, hail, rain, thunder and lightning are produced indoors, and creatures are generated in the air.

claims.quote: We have also certain chambers, which we call Chambers of Health, where we qualify the air as we think good and proper for the cure of divers diseases, and preservation of health.
claims.description: Enclosed chambers with specially adjusted air are used to treat diseases.

claims.quote: And we make (by art) in the same orchards and gardens, trees and flowers to come earlier or later than their seasons; and to come up and bear more speedily than by their natural course they do.
claims.description: Plants are forced to flower and fruit out of season and faster than nature allows.

claims.quote: We have also means to make divers plants rise by mixtures of earths without seeds; and likewise to make divers new plants, differing from the vulgar; and to make one tree or plant turn into another.
claims.description: Plants are grown from soil mixtures without seeds, and new plant species are created, including one plant turning into another.

claims.quote: By art likewise, we make them greater or taller than their kind is; and contrariwise dwarf them, and stay their growth: we make them more fruitful and bearing than their kind is
claims.description: Animals are deliberately enlarged, shrunk, or made more fertile than their natural kind.

claims.quote: We find means to make commixtures and copulations of different kinds; which have produced many new kinds, and them not barren, as the general opinion is.
claims.description: Crosses between different kinds of animals are made that produce new, fertile kinds.

claims.quote: We make a number of kinds of serpents, worms, flies, fishes, of putrefaction; whereof some are advanced (in effect) to be perfect creatures, like bests or birds; and have sexes, and do propagate.
claims.description: Living creatures are made to arise from rotting matter, and some become fully formed, reproducing animals.

claims.quote: Wherein we find many strange effects; as continuing life in them, though divers parts, which you account vital, be perished and taken forth; resuscitating of some that seem dead in appearance; and the like.
claims.description: Animals are kept alive after vital organs are removed, and some apparently dead are revived.

claims.quote: We have some meats also and breads and drinks, which taken by men enable them to fast long after; and some other, that used make the very flesh of men's bodies sensibly more hard and tough and their strength far greater than otherwise it would be.
claims.description: Foods are made that let people go long periods without eating and that make the body stronger and tougher.

claims.quote: We procure means of seeing objects afar off; as in the heaven and remote places; and represent things near as afar off; and things afar off as near; making feigned distances.
claims.description: Optical instruments bring distant objects, including celestial ones, into view and alter apparent distances.

claims.quote: We have also glasses and means to see small and minute bodies perfectly and distinctly; as the shapes and colours of small flies and worms, grains and flaws in gems, which cannot otherwise be seen, observations in urine and blood not otherwise to be seen.
claims.description: Magnifying glasses reveal tiny organisms and details in blood and urine that cannot be seen by the unaided eye.

claims.quote: We find also divers means, yet unknown to you, of producing of light originally from divers bodies.
claims.description: Light is produced from materials other than fire or heated bodies.

claims.quote: We have also means to convey sounds in trunks and pipes, in strange lines and distances.
claims.description: Sound is carried over long distances through pipes and tubes.

claims.quote: We make divers imitations of taste likewise, so that they will deceive any man's taste.
claims.description: Artificial flavors are made that fool even experienced tasters.

claims.quote: and likewise new mixtures and compositions of gun-powder, wild-fires burning in water, and unquenchable.
claims.description: New explosive and incendiary mixtures are made, including fires that burn on water and cannot be put out.

claims.quote: to make them stronger and more violent than yours are; exceeding your greatest cannons and basilisks.
claims.description: Engines and guns are built that are more powerful than the largest cannons of the time.

claims.quote: We imitate also flights of birds; we have some degrees of flying in the air.
claims.description: Machines that fly, at least to some degree, are built in imitation of birds.

claims.quote: We have ships and boats for going under water, and brooking of seas; also swimming-girdles and supporters.
claims.description: Submersible ships and boats are built that travel underwater and cross the seas beneath the surface.

claims.quote: We have divers curious clocks, and other like motions of return: and some perpetual motions.
claims.description: Perpetual motion machines are claimed to exist alongside clocks.

claims.quote: We imitate also motions of living creatures, by images, of men, beasts, birds, fishes, and serpents.
claims.description: Lifelike mechanical figures of people and animals are built that move like living creatures.

claims.quote: And we do also declare natural divinations of diseases, plagues, swarms-of hurtful creatures, scarcity, tempests, earthquakes, great inundations, comets, temperature of the year, and divers other things;
claims.description: Natural forecasts of diseases, plagues, storms, earthquakes, floods, comets and harvests are made and announced in advance.

claims.quote: We have also pools, of which some do strain fresh water out of salt; and others by art do turn fresh water into salt.
claims.description: Pools are used to turn seawater into fresh water and fresh water into salt.
